beats.text: Revenge feels sweet. Until you actually get it.
In an experiment, a player secretly cheated his group in a money game. Some players then got the chance to punish him.
Everyone who could punish him, did. And they ended up feeling worse than those who couldn't.
Both groups were sure revenge would feel good. It didn't.
Punishing kept them thinking about it. The others just moved on.
So revenge doesn't close the wound. It keeps it open.

sources: Carlsmith, Wilson & Gilbert (2008). The paradoxical consequences of revenge. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 95(6). Public-goods investment game with confederate free rider; all who could punish did; punishers felt worse than non-punishers yet predicted they'd feel better; rumination explanation. Via APA Monitor 2009.
